summary: Pole L-4 lookout near Edith Peak, Lolo NF; built 1935 per firelookout.com (earlier 1928 and 1934 newspaper mentions); planned use 1967; destroyed 1972.

facts.design: Pole tower with an L-4 cab

events.note: Daily Missoulian list of new Lolo structures names Edith Peak; the item does not say what was built.
Materials ordered for ten new towers; Edith Peak named as a Frenchtown-district location.
firelookout.com gives 1935 (one mile south of the summit). A September 1935 item mentions work at the Edith Peak lookout.
Forest Service photo dated 1953-08, catalogued as the Edith Peak fire near Ninemile.
Listed among the locations the Lolo planned to use in 1967 (planned use, not confirmed staffing).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 1935. Newspapers mention Edith Peak earlier: a 1928 list of new structures and a 1934 order of materials for a planned Frenchtown-district tower. A September 1935 item mentions the lookout. The sources do not say which 1928 structure was meant. The story gives firelookout's 1935 date and notes the earlier mentions.

notes_for_editor: Built year conflicts: 1935 (firelookout.com) against 1928 and 1934 newspaper mentions; the 1928 item is ambiguous. The 20-foot height comes only from firelookout.com's '20' pole' wording. The photo url is the Montana History Portal item page, not the image file, so the editor will need the image file if it is used. The 1967 list is planned use, not confirmed staffing. No source describes the site today, and access is not documented.
